answer_1.quote: In this paper, we focus on sentence simplification in English, which typically involves rephrasing part or all of a sentence into language which is more accessible and easier to understand.

answer_2.quote: To assess how well LLMs can perform TS, we evaluate all the model outputs using a suite of automatic metrics. We measure simplicity using SARI, meaning preservation using BERTScore, and readability using FKGL. ... Additionally, we report LENS, a recently proposed learned metric

answer_4.quote: First, we check whether or not each output is a valid simplification and highlight common failure cases such as inappropriate changes to the meaning of the original text, ungrammatical outputs, and the occurrence of hallucinations. Then, we annotate occurrences of common simplification edit operations such as lexical simplification, deletion, sentence splitting, reordering, and paraphrasing. ... all annotations were performed by one of the authors and subsequently validated by another author independently.
answer_4.guideline: Check for valid simplification by identifying failure cases (inappropriate meaning changes, ungrammaticality, hallucinations) and annotate simplification operations (lexical simplification, deletion, splitting, reordering, paraphrasing).
